book: Nutrition Through the Life Cycle (Brown), Chapter 16: Adult Nutrition and Chapter 17: Adult Nutrition: Conditions and Interventions
kicker: Lesson 9 of your course, built from Chapters 16 and 17 of your Nutrition Through the Life Cycle textbook. Test practice uses checked answers, because there is no official key for this test.

steps.title: How energy needs change in adulthood
teach: Metabolic rate and energy use start to drop in early adulthood, by about 2.0% per decade in women and 2.9% in men. This mostly follows a drop in activity and muscle. Staying active slows it down.

Resting energy expenditure (REE) can be estimated with a formula. For women: REE = (10 × weight in kg) + (6.25 × height in cm) − (5 × age) − 161. Multiply by an activity factor (for example, 1.4 for light activity) to estimate daily needs. To lose about 1 lb a week, eat about 500 fewer Calories a day.

act.prompt: A 40-year-old woman weighs 60 kg and is 165 cm tall. What is her REE? (Round to the nearest whole number.)

steps.title: Macronutrients and alcohol
teach: The adult range for fat is 20–35% of Calories. On 2,000 Calories, that's 400–700 Calories from fat. To check a food, divide the Calories from fat by total Calories and multiply by 100. Saturated fat should stay under the Daily Value of 20 g on a 2,000-Calorie diet.

A standard alcoholic drink has about 13–15 g of alcohol, or about 0.5 oz of ethanol. Sugary drinks, including fancy coffee drinks, add a lot of Calories and are linked to metabolic syndrome and fatty liver.

act.prompt: A snack has 180 Calories, 54 of them from fat. What percent of its Calories come from fat?

steps.title: Menopause
teach: After menopause, the drop in estrogen speeds up bone loss, shifts fat toward the belly and raises the risk of heart disease. Calcium, vitamin D, weight-bearing activity and a heart-healthy diet become even more important.
Fat stored deep in the belly (visceral fat) is linked to more health risks than fat under the skin or on the hips and thighs.

act.prompt: Which of these is NOT caused by lower estrogen after menopause?

options.label: Faster bone loss
options.feedback: Lower estrogen does speed up bone loss.

options.label: More belly fat
options.feedback: Fat tends to shift toward the abdomen.

options.label: More acne
options.feedback: Right. Acne isn't one of the effects described.

steps.title: Heart disease and metabolic syndrome
teach: Cardiovascular disease affects the heart, the brain (stroke) and the blood vessels. Risk factors for coronary heart disease include low HDL (under 40 mg/dL), high LDL, smoking, high blood pressure, diabetes, a family history of early heart disease, older age (55+ for women), belly fat and eating few whole grains. Fat on the hips and thighs isn't a risk factor.

Metabolic syndrome is a cluster that includes belly fat, high blood glucose, high triglycerides, low HDL and high blood pressure. Helpful changes include fewer high-fat dairy foods and fried foods, leaner meats, and more whole grains and fibre.

act.prompt: Which is NOT a risk factor for coronary heart disease?

options.label: Extra fat on the hips and thighs
options.feedback: Right. Belly fat raises risk, but hip and thigh fat doesn't.

options.label: Eating few whole grains
options.feedback: A low intake of whole grains is linked to higher risk.

steps.title: Cancer
teach: Cancer can start in any cell, but most cancers start in epithelial tissue, the cells lining the skin, lungs, gut, breast and other organs. These cells divide quickly and are most exposed to things in the environment.
Diet can raise or lower risk. Excess body fat, alcohol and processed meat raise it, while vegetables (such as cruciferous ones), fruit, whole grains and fibre are protective.

options.label: Epithelial tissue
options.feedback: Yes. These fast-dividing lining cells are most exposed to carcinogens.

options.label: Fat cells
options.feedback: Excess body fat raises risk, but most cancers start in epithelial tissue.

options.label: Bone marrow
options.feedback: Some cancers do, but most start in epithelial tissue.

flashcards.front: Decline in metabolic rate per decade
flashcards.back: About 2.0% for women and 2.9% for men.
Eat about 500 fewer Calories a day.

flashcards.front: Grams of alcohol in a drink

flashcards.back: 20 g a day on a 2,000-Calorie diet.

flashcards.front: Effects of lower estrogen after menopause
flashcards.back: Faster bone loss, more belly fat and higher heart disease risk.
The heart, the brain and the blood vessels.

flashcards.front: Not a heart disease risk factor
flashcards.back: Fat on the hips and thighs.
Belly fat, high glucose, high triglycerides, low HDL and high blood pressure.

quiz.q: The decline in estrogen production in women after menopause leads to all of the following EXCEPT:
o: All of the above occur with less estrogen.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Lower estrogen speeds bone loss, adds belly fat and raises heart disease risk, but acne isn't one of its effects.

quiz.q: To lose one pound per week, a person would need to eat ________ fewer Calories per day.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. About 3,500 Calories make a pound, and 3,500 ÷ 7 = 500 a day.

quiz.q: Metabolic rate and energy expenditure begin to decline in early adulthood at a rate of about _____ per decade for women and _____ per decade for men.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. The textbook gives 2.0% for women and 2.9% for men.

quiz.q: The Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Range for total fat intake is _____ of Calories.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. 20–35% for adults.

quiz.q: Based on the Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Ranges, someone that consumes 2000 Calories per day should aim for _______________ fat Calories/day.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. 20% of 2,000 is 400 and 35% is 700.

quiz.q: An alcoholic drink contains roughly _____ grams of alcohol or 0.5 oz of ethanol.
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Less certain: a standard drink is about 14 g of alcohol, but the textbook text doesn't give the figure. Check this one against your graded result.

quiz.q: One serving of Gardetto’s reduced-fat chips and twists snack mix contains 220 Calories, with 79 kcal from fat. Therefore, the snack mix derives _____% kcal from fat:
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. 79 ÷ 220 × 100 = 36%.

quiz.q: Using the answer from question #7, would this product fit the Acceptable Macronutrient Distribution Range for fat intake?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. 36% is just above the 20–35% range.

quiz.q:
Use the following information to answer questions 12-13.

Michelle is a 49-year-old, lightly active female who weighs 131 pounds and is 5’8” tall.
Females: REE = (10 x weight) + (6.25 x height) - (5 x age) - 161
Sedentary = 1.2
Light activity = 1.4
Moderate activity = 1.6
Very active = 1.1

What is Michelle’s resting metabolic rate?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. 131 lb = 59.5 kg and 68 in = 172.7 cm. 595 + 1,079 − 245 − 161 = about 1,270.

quiz.q:
Michelle is a 49-year-old, lightly active female who weighs 131 pounds and is 5’8” tall.
Females: REE = (10 x weight) + (6.25 x height) - (5 x age) - 161
Sedentary = 1.2
Light activity = 1.4
Moderate activity = 1.6
Very active = 1.1

What is Michelle’s estimated daily Calorie expenditure?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. 1,270 × 1.4 = about 1,780.

quiz.q: The majority of cancers develop in:
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. The textbook says most cancers develop in epithelial tissue.

quiz.q: The areas of the body affected by cardiovascular diseases include the:
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Cardiovascular disease includes heart disease, stroke and blood vessel disease.

quiz.q: Which of the following is NOT a risk factor for coronary heart disease?
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Belly fat raises risk, but hip and thigh fat doesn't.

quiz.q: Metabolic syndrome is related to a cluster of metabolic abnormalities that include:
quiz.e: Checked answer, not from an official key. Belly fat is one of the criteria. The others are the reverse of the real criteria.
